Under the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (Arts. 31–32), a treaty is interpreted in good faith according to the ordinary meaning of its terms, in their context and in light of its object and purpose. Preparatory works are only a supplementary means, used to confirm that meaning or to resolve ambiguity. Neither option in the note matches this rule exactly. If I must choose between them, the first (the parties' intention, evidenced in the preparatory works) is closer, because the second ignores the text and context.

CONFIDENCE: 90
